prompt.context: Your client is Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC), a state agency tasked with economic development for the state of Michigan. Michigan is still recovering from the economic recession in 2009, when Michigan had the highest unemployment rate in the country at 13.4% and also the highest net emigration, with over 86,000 citizens leaving the state, presumably to find work elsewhere. Five years later the state is slowly recovering and MEDC wants to know what to do to make Michigan more attractive.
prompt.question: What should MEDC do to make Michigan more attractive?

clarifying_info.a: The primary goal is to increase employment. A secondary goal is to increase capital expenditure (CAPEX) in the state.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any specific targets for jobs or CAPEX?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — MEDC is focused on adding 1,000 jobs and bringing in $40MM in CAPEX in the next year.

clarifying_info.q: Does MEDC have any funds to deploy?
clarifying_info.a: The state has created a special fund of $10MM for MEDC to use at its sole discretion to incentivize companies to relocate to Michigan.

exhibits.title: Projects Under Consideration
exhibits.shows: A table listing four candidate projects with their industry, number of direct jobs, and CAPEX (in $MM).

exhibits.title: Job Multipliers by Industry
exhibits.shows: A table showing indirect-job multiplier and induced-job multiplier for each industry type.

framework: Offer financial incentives — relocation subsidies, tax credits for expansion
Make policy/regulatory changes — streamline regulations, reform tax code, improve quality of life (education, healthcare, crime)
Create workforce programs — training programs (public and private), public works programs
Research competition — benchmark what other states do to attract business and talent

questions.prompt: Beyond financial incentives, what additional ideas could MEDC pursue to add 1,000 jobs and $40MM in CAPEX?
questions.guidance: Candidate should quickly generate at least 5 additional ideas not in their initial framework (e.g., university partnerships, infrastructure investment, targeted industry clusters, marketing campaigns, streamlined permitting). Accept a strong list or a concrete next-step pivot.

questions.prompt: Using the $10MM fund, calculate total jobs (direct + indirect + induced) for each of the four projects.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the multipliers correctly. Key trick: indirect jobs = (indirect multiplier - 1) x direct jobs; induced jobs = (induced multiplier - 1) x direct jobs. Strong candidates notice relationships between multipliers to speed calculations.

math.setup: Total jobs = Direct + Indirect + Induced. Indirect jobs = (Indirect multiplier - 1) x Direct jobs. Induced jobs = (Induced multiplier - 1) x Direct jobs.
steps: Gamer Zone (Software, 100 direct): Indirect = (4.2-1)*100 = 320; Induced = (2.6-1)*100 = 160; Total = 100+320+160 = 580
Speedylane (Call Center, 520 direct): Indirect = (1.1-1)*520 = 52; Induced = (1.05-1)*520 = 26; Total = 520+52+26 = 598
math.answer: Gamer Zone: 580 total jobs, $70MM CAPEX | Kidoodle: 448 total jobs, $16MM CAPEX | PreFab: 560 total jobs, $420MM CAPEX | Speedylane: 598 total jobs, $4MM CAPEX

questions.prompt: Which single project best achieves MEDC's dual goals of 1,000 jobs and $40MM CAPEX, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first eliminate Kidoodle ($16MM CAPEX, below $40MM target) and Speedylane ($4MM CAPEX, far below target). Then compare Gamer Zone (580 jobs, $70MM CAPEX) vs. PreFab (560 jobs, $420MM CAPEX). A strong candidate builds a comparison framework (jobs vs. CAPEX, permanence, risk, quality of jobs) and makes a recommendation. Concerns/benefits per project: Gamer Zone — software developers are highly educated/white collar; smaller CAPEX could mean less permanence; availability of trained employees may be limited; may locate in already prosperous area. PreFab — very high CAPEX suggests permanence and significant capital commitment; highest potential to spur indirect/induced job creation; however manufacturing projects are highly competitive across states and may demand even larger incentives.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional ideas could MEDC pursue (beyond its framework) to add jobs and attract capital?

categories.name: Financial Incentives
ideas: Tax abatements for new entrants
Grants or low-interest loans for R&D
Enterprise zones with reduced tax rates
CAPEX matching grants

categories.name: Workforce Development
ideas: Community college partnerships for technical training
Apprenticeship programs with anchor employers
Retraining programs for displaced manufacturing workers
Incentives for universities to place graduates locally

categories.name: Policy & Regulatory
ideas: Streamlined business permitting and licensing
Right-to-work legislation review
Improved infrastructure (roads, broadband, utilities)
Reduce corporate tax rate selectively for target industries

categories.name: Quality of Life
ideas: Invest in public education and school quality
Crime reduction initiatives
Healthcare access improvements
Cultural and recreational amenity investment to retain talent

categories.name: Marketing & Outreach
ideas: Targeted campaigns to attract Silicon Valley overflow
Benchmarking competing state incentive packages
Trade missions to court foreign direct investment
Public-private partnerships with site selectors

recommendation: Recommend awarding the $10MM incentive fund to PreFab (capital-intensive manufacturing), which generates 560 total jobs and $420MM in CAPEX — far exceeding the $40MM CAPEX target and coming close to the 1,000-job goal when combined with other initiatives.
Alternatively, Gamer Zone is a strong second choice with 580 total jobs and $70MM CAPEX, and brings high-quality white-collar employment to the state.
risks: PreFab: Manufacturing sites attract aggressive incentive competition from other states; the high indirect-jobs multiplier signals dependence on a supplier ecosystem that may not yet exist in Michigan.
Gamer Zone: Smaller CAPEX ($70MM vs. $420MM) could mean less permanence; availability of qualified software talent in Michigan may be limited.
Neither project alone achieves the 1,000-job target — MEDC will need complementary initiatives.
next_steps: Negotiate with PreFab (or Gamer Zone) on site location to maximize spillover into high-unemployment areas.
Launch a parallel workforce training program to ensure local talent can fill the direct and indirect positions.
Monitor job-creation milestones quarterly and tie future incentive tranches to verified employment benchmarks.
Benchmark competing state offers to calibrate the $10MM commitment and avoid over-incentivizing.
